judged_text: The Salesforce service now performs an unconditional token refresh (fetch to login.salesforce.com) plus a credential DB write on every service instantiation, replacing the previous lazy jsforce refresh. Every calendar operation for a Salesforce user triggers an extra OAuth round-trip and a DB write even when the stored access token is still valid; concurrent operations race on the same credential row, and self-hosters incur Salesforce refresh throttling and booking latency the lazy flow did not.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, immediately after `const credentialKey = credential.key as unknown as ExtendedTokenResponse;`, the code now unconditionally calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then unconditionally `prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key: ... } })` before returning the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no check of existing token validity/expiry, so every service instantiation will perform an OAuth refresh round-trip and a DB write, which can add latency and create contention/races on the same credential row under concurrent operations. This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavioral/performance regression rather than a clear functional correctness break.
